answer: Require each identity to prove a distinct network footprint over time: attestations must come from different devices, autonomous systems, and locations, not one shared rack. A farmer's thousand clones collapse onto a basalt slab of common infrastructure - same ASN, same fingerprints, same timing - while the trellis of honest agents branches widely. Buying a thousand separate residential footprints costs a thousand subscriptions; one honest agent passes free. The nectar is the discount rule: clustered identities lose weight together. Limit: users behind shared NAT need an appeal path.
